title: Smart home remote with undo
description: A smart home remote can already turn lights on and off and supports undo — but RemoteControl is tightly coupled to Light. It uses instanceof checks to decide what to do and tracks action names as strings to reverse them. Fix it so RemoteControl only depends on the Command interface, then implement LightOnCommand and LightOffCommand so the logic moves into the command classes where it belongs.
hints: Once fixed, RemoteControl should have no reference to Light at all — only a Deque<Command> history
pressButton(Command) should call command.execute() and push the command onto history
pressUndo() should pop the last command and call undo() on it — no string checks needed
LightOnCommand.execute() calls light.turnOn(); undo() calls light.turnOff()
issues: RemoteControl uses instanceof to inspect each command type — adding any new command means editing RemoteControl
Undo tracks action names as strings instead of delegating back to the command, so the logic is duplicated
overallGoal: Use the Command pattern so RemoteControl works with any command through the Command interface without knowing about any specific device.
goals: Remove the Light field from RemoteControl and replace the string history with a Deque<Command>
Implement LightOnCommand: store the Light, call turnOn() in execute() and turnOff() in undo()
Implement LightOffCommand: the mirror — call turnOff() in execute() and turnOn() in undo()
In pressButton(), call command.execute() and push onto history; in pressUndo(), pop and call undo()
